overall_summary: The channel's growth is heavily driven by exotic space mysteries and extreme exoplanet physics, which consistently capture the highest views and engagement. Conversely, generic psychology and brain-fact videos are severely underperforming, with multiple re-uploads failing to gain traction, indicating audience fatigue or algorithmic suppression of these saturated topics.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet of Burning Ice' (1,055 views), 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' (996 views), and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (660 views) are the channel's top-performing videos.
winning_patterns.action: Produce a dedicated series focusing on the most extreme, terrifying, and bizarre exoplanets in the known universe, emphasizing highly visual weather and atmospheric anomalies.

winning_patterns.pattern: Mind-Bending Relativity Applied to the Body
winning_patterns.evidence: 'Why Your Head Is Older Than Your Feet' achieved 263 views, significantly outperforming standard anatomy or psychology content.
winning_patterns.action: Frame physics and time-dilation concepts through a personal, human-centric lens to make complex science immediately relatable and shocking.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' failed across three separate uploads (5, 8, and 53 views), and 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' stalled at 17 views.
weak_patterns.action: Halt production on generic cognitive psychology facts and redirect creative resources toward cosmic scale mysteries and physics paradoxes.

weak_patterns.evidence: Re-uploading the 'Fake Memories' short multiple times with minor tweaks yielded near-zero views each time.
weak_patterns.action: Establish a rule where a failed concept is completely rewritten with a new hook and visual style rather than re-uploading the same asset.

next_video.concept: The Planet Where It Rains Rocks: CoRoT-7b
next_video.opening_direction: Imagine a world where the weather forecast calls for a literal storm of rocks.
next_video.twist_direction: Because this planet is tidally locked, one side is a boiling ocean of liquid lava, while the other side is cold enough to snow solid sodium.
next_video.reason: Leverages the proven high-performance pattern of extreme exoplanet weather (similar to the ruby and molten iron rain videos) and targets the successful early afternoon posting window.

experiment: Test a cinematic 'What-If' space survival scenario, such as 'What if you stood on the surface of a planet made of burning ice?', to merge the dominant exoplanet theme with immersive, first-person storytelling.
